THIS BAIL APPLICATION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 19.10.2023, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 B.A.No.8473/2023 2  ORDER
This is an application for regular bail 2.

The petitioner is the first accused in Crime No.2/2021 of Vanitha Police Station, Malappuram District, alleging commission of offences under Sections 376(3), 354(I)

1 (i) of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 5(l)(n) r/w 6(1)(2) and 9(l)(m)(n) r/w 10 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO Act), 2012.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. The allegation against the petitioner (who is stated to be the step-father of the minor victim) is that the petitioner sexually abused the minor victim and committed penetrative sexual assault on her and thereby he committed the offences alleged against him.
The petitioner was granted bail in Crime No.2/2021 by Annexure-2 order.

However, that order granting bail has been cancelled and the petitioner has again been remanded, on account of the fact that yet another crime namely Crime No.5/2023 of the very same Police Station has been registered against the petitioner, stating that the petitioner again committed the offence as against the very same victim while on bail in Crime No.2/2021.
4.
The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner has been in custody from 08-01-2023 in connection with the second case registered against him.

It is submitted that while in custody in connection with the second case, the bail granted to the petitioner through Annexure-2 order was also cancelled, essentially on the finding that the petitioner has committed a similar offence while on bail.

It is submitted that the allegation that the petitioner has committed a similar offence while on bail is completely false and a false allegation has been raised only on account of certain issues between the petitioner and the mother of the victim.

It is also submitted that the victim, who was in the care and custody of the Child Welfare Committee, claims that she had been subjected to rape by the petitioner on the second occasion while she had come home during vacation.
It is submitted that there are no proceedings of the Child Welfare Committee to indicate that the victim was permitted to go home during vacations.
It is submitted that this is fatal to the prosecution case.
5. The learned Senior Public Prosecutor would submit that the petitioner is clearly not entitled to bail.
It is submitted that there is a clear finding that the petitioner had committed a similar offence while on bail in the first case.
It is submitted that this ground is sufficient to hold that the petitioner cannot be granted bail.
It is also submitted that the safety of the victim has to be ensured for examination during trial and this cannot be permitted to be defeated by releasing the petitioner on bail.

6. Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Senior Public Prosecutor, I am of the view that the petitioner cannot be granted bail in Crime No.2/2021 of Vanitha Police Station, Malappuram district, which is now pending as S.C.No.608/2021 on the file of the Special Court for the Trial of Offences under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offices Act, Manjeri.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offices Act, Manjeri
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The allegations against the petitioner are serious.
That apart, there is a clear finding that the petitioner committed a similar offence while on bail.
The victim is none other than the step-daughter of the petitioner.
Therefore, if the petitioner is granted bail, the safety of the victim is also at stake.
Therefore, the bail application will stand dismissed.

However, considering the fact that the petitioner has been in custody for a long time and also considering the fact that the first case registered against the petitioner is pending as S.C.No.608/2021 on the file of the Special Court for V.Kannan vs State Of Kerala on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40839911/
2 the Trial of Offences under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offices Act, Manjeri, from the year 2021, a direction can be issued to the Special Court to expedite the trial of S.C.No.608/2021.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offices Act, Manjeri
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Accordingly, there will be a direction to the Special Court for the Trial of Offences under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offices Act, Manjeri, to expedite the trial of S.C.No.608/2021,
considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also considering the fact that the petitioner has been in custody for a considerably long period.
